findings.reason: §5 should name and extend `_figure_retention` rather than describe a new gate and defer the invariant to another plan.
findings.text: §5 states the rotation invariant by reference to a companion plan's reaper, but the test it needs already exists as `_figure_retention` in `reckon/crew/routing.py:1312`, which tells "recorded" from "explicitly-absent" from "missing" and is precisely the "do not delete detail whose derived figure was never computed" check

findings.reason: the section must cite the existing index mechanism it extends (or say why none can be) before proposing a rebuilt index, or it will ship a third one.
findings.text: §7 node 2 proposes "the index … rebuilt from the files, with an equal answer set" as if it were new, but two such indexes already exist: `reckon/metadata_index.py` is the repo's established "index derived from files, persisted under a cache root, rebuilt on demand" pattern, and `reckon/ledger.py:786 _run_index_path` already builds a per-project index from the run files

findings.reason: the section must name `reckon/ledger.py:786` as the index owner to extend, or state why a second SQLite index beside it is needed, or the two will drift and a reader will get different answers from the index the plan names and the index the code uses.
findings.text: §7 makes the SQLite store the index over the per-run files, but `reckon/ledger.py:786 _run_index_path` already derives an index (`cache/ledger-<sha>.sqlite`) from those same files and is the one `ledger.load`/`indexed_headers` read through, so the design leaves two indexes owning one history

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2's embedded store hides its schema, five query indexes, insert and migration behind a small append/compare/import interface (`reckon/run_store.py`), and §7 keeps `ledger.append_run`/`ledger.load` as the record interface over the per-run files, so the design's interface is smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §7 re-designates the SQLite store as "an index derived from [the per-run files]", but `reckon/ledger.py:786 _run_index_path` already builds exactly such an index over the same rows, and §7 names neither it nor `reckon/run_store.py` as the owner to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; the live sections (§5 rotation, the open `detail-horizon` decision) add no CLI option, MCP view, or refusal family, and §7's `ledger.append_run`/`ledger.load` and its duplicate-promotion refusal already exist in `reckon/ledger.py`, so nothing new is added without being accounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §5's rotation invariant ("nothing removed before the figures derived from it exist") is already owned by `reckon/crew/routing.py:1312 _figure_retention`, and §7's "an index derived from the [per-run files] and rebuilt on demand" already exists twice over, in `reckon/metadata_index.py` and `reckon/ledger.py:786 _run_index_path`; the plan cites none of the three.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §7 does not wrap the existing readers; it re-points `ledger.load` and the `runs` reader at the per-run files, which is an extension of the existing reader rather than a parallel one.
